title: How To Solve It With Code—background on the course; a discussion with Jeremy and Hamel
summary: Jeremy Howard and Hamel Husain introduce a course and tool built on small interactive steps with AI, arguing non-coders hit walls with one-shot generation.

assertions.quote: they've gone from zero to mark five and then the kids like oh thanks Dad that's nice but when I click this button

verdicts.note: Unreviewed AI-built apps commonly ship with security, scaling and maintainability problems; prototypes are their sweet spot.

assertions.quote: you do actually need to learn to code

verdicts.note: Basic coding helps people direct and check AI output, and adoption among non-engineers is growing. The labor-market payoff for non-engineers is still unproven.

assertions.quote: when you build the code up slowly you end up much faster than the person who does it 200 at a time

verdicts.note: Small batches with fast feedback are a strong DORA predictor of delivery performance; DORA 2024 linked AI to larger batches and lower stability.

assertions.quote: it just ends up being overly complicated and not really customized for your particular problem

verdicts.note: GitClear and DORA 2025 data show more churn and duplication and lower delivery stability as AI adoption rises; more code means more to maintain.

assertions.quote: getting into this bigger and bigger hole of technical debt as it writes more and more code that you don't understand

verdicts.note: Unreviewed, fast AI output does accumulate debt (GitClear duplication, churn), but debt depends on review discipline, not on whether AI was used per se.

assertions.quote: make sure you really understand that that code and why it's written that way and what it does

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 study found high scorers used AI for conceptual questions and explanations while low scorers delegated; small sample and a single learning task.

assertions.quote: the level of difficulty of problem that you're able to solve and the complexity that the AI can solve is much higher

verdicts.note: Consistent with evidence for incremental verification, but no controlled comparison of this workflow exists.

Iterative use (adapt, improve, debug, or the ideate-adapt-debug sequence) improved accuracy at some speed cost, while one-shot direct acceptance did not improve accuracy. The evidence is correlational and on simple tasks.

assertions.quote: Google CEO said that most recent the most recent few months 25% of their code is generated by AI

verdicts.note: Google and Microsoft executives cite ~25-50% of new code AI-generated; the figures are self-reported and usually count accepted suggestions, not finished code.
